label: Injection
detail: Large plants usually connect to transmission through step-up transformers; smaller generators can connect to distribution.

label: Transfer
detail: Transmission supplies distribution substations, where transformers step down the voltage.

label: Delivery
detail: Local wires carry power to customers, whoever supplies their electricity.

label: Supply charge
detail: Customers pay for electricity supply, sometimes on the same bill as utility delivery charges.

label: Delivery charge
detail: Delivery charges fund local network service and can include transmission and other regulated costs.

label: Wholesale purchases
detail: Suppliers buy wholesale electricity; some purchases settle through ISO/RTO markets and others through bilateral contracts.

label: Generator revenue
detail: Generators receive payments for energy and, where applicable, capacity and grid services. Bilateral sales may settle separately.

label: Network service charges
detail: A distribution utility may pay for transmission service as a network customer. Other arrangements charge the supplier or another load-serving entity.

label: Transmission tariff credits
detail: In PJM, network transmission charges are credited to transmission owners to recover their approved revenue requirements.

label: Buys generation equipment
detail: Generation companies buy turbines, generators, inverters and other plant equipment.

label: Buys transmission gear
detail: Transmission utilities buy transformers, breakers, conductors and other network equipment.

label: Buys distribution gear
detail: Distribution utilities buy transformers, poles, switches and meters.

label: FERC fees
detail: FERC recovers its regular operating budget through annual charges and filing fees on regulated companies. Transmission utilities are one example.

label: State PUC fees
detail: Utilities pay assessments that fund state regulators, often recovered in customer bills. Rules vary by state.

label: ISO/RTO operating fees
detail: Market and transmission customers pay tariff-based fees that fund ISO/RTO operations, shown here through settlements.

label: Owns, maintains, operates
detail: Generation companies own plant equipment; operations and maintenance may be contracted out. ISO/RTOs coordinate dispatch.

label: Owns, maintains, operates
detail: Transmission owners maintain equipment and perform switching, coordinated with the ISO/RTO.

label: Owns, maintains, operates
detail: Distribution utilities operate and maintain local equipment and restore service after outages.

label: Dispatch instructions
detail: The ISO/RTO sends participating generators output targets; plant operators run the equipment.

label: Regional grid coordination
detail: The ISO/RTO coordinates regional transmission reliability and outages; owners maintain and physically operate the equipment.

label: Runs market & billing
detail: The ISO/RTO runs organized wholesale markets and handles their settlements and applicable transmission billing.

label: FERC oversight
detail: FERC approves ISO/RTO tariffs and market rules. Reliability standards also involve NERC and regional entities.

label: Transmission rates (FERC)
detail: FERC approves transmission rates and tariffs for the public utilities shown here.

label: Distribution rates (states)
detail: State commissions approve distribution rates for investor-owned utilities. Publicly owned and cooperative utilities may have different oversight.

label: Retail supplier rules (states)
detail: States set licensing and consumer-protection rules for competitive retail electricity suppliers.

label: Electricity supply contract
detail: The supplier arranges the customer’s electricity supply; the local utility provides physical delivery.
